CRITICAL ANTI-TEXT DIRECTIVE: ZERO text of ANY kind. No letters, words, numbers, runes, hieroglyphs, symbols, UI text, watermarks, logos. Use ONLY abstract fracture patterns for decorative markings.

CRITICAL: NO HALO RINGS. No circular discs behind head. No glowing rings.
CRITICAL: NO ANIMALS AT FEET. No companion animals, no creatures. Energy/void patterns only.
CRITICAL: THE HOLLOW IS NOT A PLAYABLE DEITY. This creature must look INCOMPLETE, FRACTURED, CORRUPTED. Where deities radiate divine light, this creature ABSORBS light. Where deities are alive, this creature is ABSENCE. Where deities have faces, this creature has broken or missing masks.
CRITICAL: HOLLOW AESTHETIC — charcoal-black void-stuff body (pure absence given form, NOT metal, NOT stone, NOT flesh). White fracture cracks (cold white lines where light dies, NOT warm energy, NOT fire). Incomplete or broken masks. Broken Gate stone embedded in body (fragments of the original Mythos Gates fused into the form). Negative-space wounds (holes showing ACTIVE NOTHING, the void that consumes). Anti-light seams (absolute black that drinks surrounding light). Ash falling UPWARD (gravity inverts around Hollow creatures).
CRITICAL: NOT EVIL, NOT DEMONIC — the Hollow is EROSION, not malice. It is absence, not corruption with intent. It should feel like looking at a wound in reality, not at a villain. Cold, silent, erasing, not raging or screaming.
CRITICAL: EPIC SCALE — this creature is large but SMALLER than deities. Deities are colossal (hundreds of feet tall). This creature is large enemy scale (20-40 feet tall). Low camera angle looking up. Show the creature emerging from a Gate fracture or void breach in the ground.
CRITICAL: Readable tactical RPG silhouette — the creature must be readable as a BRUISER unit at a glance. Clear weapon or threat indicator. Distinct silhouette from all other Hollow creatures.

Create Hollow Oath-Eater, for Mythos Gates: Ascension. The Hollow threat faction.
Faction: The Hollow (non-playable threat faction).
Threat Tier: Major.
Creature Category: Hollow Creature.
Combat Role: BRUISER.
Canon: The Hollow is the anti-civilization that grows in the wound between Realms. It is what the Mythos Gates were built to keep sealed. When the Gates broke, the Hollow came through. This creature carries fragments of broken Gate stone in its body — not as armor, but as the scar of its own creation. Where deities are alive, this creature is absence. Where deities radiate, this creature absorbs.

ART STYLE: Premium dark mythological tactical RPG enemy concept art. Grim dark aesthetic. The Hollow should feel WRONG — like looking at something that should not exist. Not scary in a monster way, but unsettling in an existential way. This is not a demon or a beast — it is a WOUND IN REALITY wearing a shape it stole from something that was real. Painterly textures, deep shadows, void-black depths.

HOLLOW OATH-EATER — A heavy black beast-knight that devours sacred oaths.

BODY: Heavy, massive humanoid-beast hybrid — 25-30 feet. NOT a clean humanoid — something between a knight and a beast, WRONG in its proportions. The body is dense charcoal-black void-stuff, but THICK, compressed, like absence given weight. The shoulders are too broad, the torso too deep, the arms too heavy. It moves like a knight but is built like a predator. Negative-space wounds across the torso show ACTIVE NOTHING inside — the void that consumes.

MASK: A ringed jaw — the mask is a broken ring/halo fragment fused to the lower face, forming a gaping maw where a mouth should be. The ring is a broken piece of a divine halo (taken from a consumed deity) bent into a jaw shape. Inside the ring-jaw: white crack-teeth, fractured and jagged, NOT bone, NOT enamel, but broken reality fragments that serve as teeth. The upper face is smooth void-stuff, no eyes, no nose — just the ring-jaw gaping.

CHEST: An oath-stone is lodged in the center of the chest — a large, dark stone tablet covered in ERASING runes. The runes are visible but fading, like text being scrubbed away. The stone is embedded deep, fused to the void-stuff body. Cold white anti-light bleeds from around the stone's edges — the Oath-Eater is consuming the oath written on the stone, and the anti-light is the visible sign of consumption.

ARMS: Massive arms ending in heavy void-stuff fists. Torn rune-chains wrap around the forearms — broken chains of dark metal, each link inscribed with fading runes. The chains are NOT functional — they are remnants of oaths that bound this creature before it consumed them. The chains hang loose, broken, trailing.

POSE: Standing massive, head lowered, fists clenched, chains dragging. Not charging — WAITING. The pose of something that has just consumed and is ready to consume again. The ring-jaw should be slightly open, showing the crack-teeth inside.

SCALE: 25-30 feet. Low camera angle, looking up at the massive form. Broken rubble and Gate fragments at its feet. The Oath-Eater should look HEAVY — the opposite of the thin, stretched Hollow forms.

GROUND: The ground around the Oath-Eater is CRACKED with white fracture lines — not anti-light, but the actual ground breaking under the weight of its absence. Torn rune-fragments scattered. Ash falling upward. The earth looks like it is being CRUSHED by the creature's void-weight.

BACKGROUND: Dark void environment. Distant broken Gate-arches. The atmosphere should feel HEAVY — oppressive, crushing, like standing in a room where all the air has been replaced by nothing. Palette: charcoal-black, dark grey, cold white, faint oath-stone brown-grey.

VFX: Torn rune-chains trailing and swaying. Cold white anti-light bleeding from the oath-stone. White crack-teeth catching anti-light. Heavy void-pressure — the air around the Oath-Eater looks compressed, bent, HEAVY. Ash falling upward but slower than smaller Hollow creatures — gravity struggles against this one.

SILHOUETTE: Heavy, massive, jaw-forward. Reads as a bruiser/tank unit — large, heavy, threatening. The ring-jaw and massive fists are the primary identifiers. Distinct from all other Hollow creatures — this one is BUILT, not thin.
